name: Brake caliper
summary: The clamp that holds the brake pads and squeezes them against the disc when you press the pedal.
whatItDoes: The caliper turns fluid pressure from the brake pedal into a strong clamping force on the disc.
howItWorks: Pressing the pedal pushes brake fluid through the brake lines. That fluid pushes a piston (or several) out of the caliper, forcing the pads onto the disc. Most cars use a 'floating' caliper: one piston pushes the inner pad, and the caliper body slides on guide pins to pull the outer pad in. The caliper is held by a bracket bolted to the steering knuckle.
failureSymptoms: The car pulls to one side when braking
One wheel much hotter than the others after a drive (sticking caliper)
Brake fluid leaking at the wheel
safetyNotes: Never let the caliper hang by its rubber brake hose. Support it with a hook or wire.
Brake fluid damages paint and irritates skin and eyes. Wear gloves and eye protection.
If you open the hydraulic system, the brakes must be bled before driving.
